prompt:
# Subject Merge Fine Clustering

## Quick Start

Inside one topic area, create tight candidate clusters that are worth a later same-concept decision. Use only the provided candidate cards.

## Identity Filter

Cluster candidates only when they might be the same teachable idea at the same level, testable with the same question.

Do not cluster just because candidates share a keyword. Keep candidates separate when one adds implementation, math, limitation, application, deeper mechanism, tool-specific behavior, or a broader/narrower student action.

Doubt means singleton. Under-clustering is safer than sending unrelated candidates to merge evaluation.

## Output

Return one JSON object only:

```json
{
  "clusters": [
    {
      "id": "cluster_001",
      "label": "Short candidate cluster",
      "rationale": "Why these candidates may share concept identity.",
      "candidate_ids": ["candidate-id"]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Self-Check

- Every input candidate ID appears exactly once.
- Each non-singleton cluster has a plausible same-concept reason.
- Implementation, limitation, application, math, and deeper-revisit candidates were not grouped with definitions just because labels overlap.
- Mixed-language same-level candidates were clustered when their teachable idea matches.
- No web search or external knowledge was used.

area.label: Feature Extraction Pipelines and APIs
area.rationale: End-to-end feature extraction, comparison of approaches, and serving NLP models via Flask APIs.

candidates.label: Feature Extraction in NLP
candidates.description: The process of transforming cleaned text into numerical features that machine learning algorithms can process, a fundamental step in NLP pipelines.
coverage_criteria: Explain why text needs to be converted to numbers for ML models.
List common feature extraction methods (e.g., BoW, TF-IDF, embeddings).
Describe the role of feature extraction in an NLP pipeline.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: Implementing Feature Extraction in Python for NLP
candidates.description: Practical implementation of NLP feature extraction pipelines using Python libraries such as scikit-learn, NLTK, and spaCy, including loading text data and applying methods like CountVectorizer.
coverage_criteria: Can write code that loads text data and applies a feature extraction method (e.g., using scikit-learn's CountVectorizer).
Can describe common Python libraries used for NLP feature extraction.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: Building a Python Web API to Serve NLP Models
candidates.description: Developing a Python-based web API to serve NLP models, using frameworks like Flask or FastAPI, including steps to wrap a model into a REST endpoint and considerations like latency and data serialization.
coverage_criteria: Can outline steps to wrap an NLP model into a simple REST API using Python.
Can identify challenges in serving NLP models via APIs (e.g., latency, data serialization).
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: Creating a Basic Flask API Endpoint
candidates.description: Setting up a minimal Flask application by importing Flask, creating an instance, defining a route with @app.route to bind a view function that returns data (e.g., JSON), and running the app. This forms the basis for a simple API endpoint.
coverage_criteria: Can write a minimal Flask app that defines a route returning a string or JSON.
Can explain how the @app.route decorator registers a URL endpoint.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: Handling Dynamic URL Parameters and URL Generation in Flask
candidates.description: Using Flask's variable rules to capture dynamic parts of a URL (e.g., <int:user_id>) and employing url_for() to generate URLs for view functions, promoting maintainable and flexible endpoint design.
coverage_criteria: Can write a route with a dynamic path segment and enforce type with converters.
Can use url_for() to generate a URL to a given view function, including passing arguments.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: Defining API endpoints with HTTP methods in Flask
candidates.description: Specify allowed HTTP methods with the methods argument to @app.route; use request.method to branch, or use shortcut decorators @app.get/@app.post.
coverage_criteria: Can create a route that handles both GET and POST
Can use request.method to distinguish request types
Can rewrite using separate @app.get and @app.post decorators
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidate_assignment_rule: Cluster only. Every input candidate ID must appear exactly once across clusters. Prefer tight clusters; topic overlap alone is not a cluster.

web_access_policy.instruction: Do not use web search or open URLs. Use only the provided candidate cards.
